finding.claim: Broken admin authorization on POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban: the except Exception block swallows the 403 raised by require_admin (abort(403) raises a werkzeug HTTPException, which subclasses Exception), logs a warning, and falls through to do_ban(uid), so any authenticated non-admin can ban any user.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled request to POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban by a logged-in non-admin account (g.user is a mapping with a falsy or missing is_admin). The uid path parameter is also attacker-chosen.
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, a privileged state-changing operation protected by require_admin.

trace.note: Route POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban is registered with no auth decorator or policy on the route itself.
require_admin(g.user) is called with the non-admin user.
user.get('is_admin') is falsy, so line 11 executes abort(403).
abort(403) raises werkzeug Forbidden, an Exception subclass, so the failure is raised as an exception.
except Exception catches the Forbidden. There is no re-raise and no return.
Only a warning is logged. Execution continues.
do_ban(uid) runs unconditionally, so the ban is applied.
Response returns jsonify(ok=True), a success response to the non-admin caller.

finding.guards_checked: (1) require_admin at admin.py:9-11 does enforce the check, but its exception is swallowed at line 18. (2) No before_request or decorator-level auth is visible in this file, so the only gate is the swallowed check. (3) The unban handler at admin.py:24-28 calls require_admin without a try block, so its 403 propagates correctly; it is not affected. (4) Edge case checked: if g.user is missing or None, line 19 g.user.get raises AttributeError inside the except block, so the request returns 500 and do_ban is not reached. The bypass therefore requires an authenticated non-admin user object to be present in g.user. (5) Impact caveat: do_ban is a stub (pass) in this file, so the real impact depends on its implementation elsewhere. Whether g.user is populated from a trusted source is outside this file and was not verified; the defect holds regardless, because the admin check itself is ineffective.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) is the only authorization check. It raises via abort(403) rather than returning a bool, so the failure is an exception. That exception is caught by the bare `except Exception` at admin.py:18, which only logs (line 19) and does not re-raise or return. do_ban(uid) at line 20 then runs unconditionally. No before_request hook or route decorator is visible in admin.py. The unban route (lines 24-28) calls require_admin without a try block, which confirms the guard works there and makes the swallow in ban() the defect.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: require_admin's abort(403) at admin.py:11 is caught by the bare `except Exception` at admin.py:18, and execution falls through to do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20. Any caller with a g.user mapping that lacks a truthy is_admin (admin.py:10) reaches the ban, and the unban route at admin.py:26 shows the check is meant to block that path.
